headline: 1970s Stedwick closets, Whetstone paths, and why Lakeforest-era vents were never resized
description: Montgomery Village, MD is a 1970s planned community next to Gaithersburg. why lake-side townhome ducts collect pollen and old-closet lint.

sections.heading: Montgomery Village is not Gaithersburg. The closets are older.
paragraphs: Stedwick, Whetstone, East Village, the lakes, and the streets that used to orbit Lakeforest went up as a 1970s planned community next to Gaithersburg. The stock is townhomes and colonials from that build-out, plus later infill. Mechanical closets are tight. Dryer vents were run for machines that no longer exist. HOA paths keep lots leafy — and the returns keep pulling that leaf grit.
Lake-side humidity is the other half. Cool lower-level trunks sweat in Maryland summers. Pollen from the original tree plan sticks.

sections.heading: A 1970s dryer run is a fire and humidity problem
paragraphs: The original vent was sized for a smaller machine. Lint packs at elbows you cannot see without pulling the unit. Heat and moisture dump into a closet that already sits over sweating trunks. Registers look clean after you wipe them and gray again when the AC cycles.
If the lower level smells musty, when you are ready to book, use the [Montgomery Village, MD location page](/locations/montgomery-village).

sections.heading: Typical signs in a Montgomery Village townhome
listItems: Musty air from a lake-side lower level in July.
Leaf-season grit on supplies along Stedwick or Whetstone paths.
A dryer that needs two cycles in a 1970s closet.
